value: OWN-POOL UND GHOST RE-SWEEP, MEASURED 2026-08-31 (this date is part of the finding: the previous negative result rotted in under three hours). RESULT: 10 own-pool UND ghosts across 3 TUs, NOT zero. This REFUTES the summary sentence of claim.flip-ranking-table-and-corrected-own-pool-screen.20260831.v1 ('IMAGE-WIDE RESULT OF THAT SCREEN: ZERO of the 59 NonMatching TUs carry an own-pool UND ghost ... mb_tree was the only instance and it is fixed. No future flip-readiness pass needs to re-run the source-text grep'). That record's SCREEN DEFINITION is sound and was re-run unchanged; only its RESULT was wrong, and it was already contradicted the same day by claim.sysservice-data-gap-closed-and-own-pool-und-ghosts-found.20260901.v1 for one TU. The correct standing statement is the one below, WITH ITS DATE. FINDINGS BY TU. (1) game/g3d/auxanim: FIVE ghosts (lbl_803459B8/BC/D0/D8/E0) - ALL FIXED, see attempt.auxanim-own-pool-ghosts-and-sdata2-order.20260831.v1. This TU was NOT merely a naming defect: because the source imported 255.0 as `extern f64 lbl_803459E0` instead of spelling it, MWCC never emitted that pool entry at all, so our .sdata2 was 48 bytes against the target's 56 and the unit's data score was capped at 69.07%. Converting the ghosts to literals made .sdata2 BYTE-IDENTICAL (56 bytes) and took the unit to 83.51% data; project Data +56 bytes. (2) game/sys/sysservice: THREE ghosts (lbl_80117708/770/790) - NOT TOUCHED, correctly: work_claim.flip-stragglers.20260831.v1 (worker FG) explicitly owns this TU and names these three ghosts in its scope. Confirmed still present. (3) game/world/btricol: TWO ghosts (lbl_80345D40 f64 0.0, lbl_80345D50 f32 0.0f) - BLOCKED, and this is the most important new finding, recorded in full below. BTRICOL IS A FALSE FLIP CANDIDATE. The flip-ranking record lists game/world/btricol among the TEN TUs sitting at exactly one non-exact function (BTriLineCol, 1800B, data 100%), i.e. a top flip target. It cannot flip. Both of its own-pool ghosts are referenced from WEBFRANK-PINNED functions whose source is hash-frozen: lbl_80345D40 is read at btricol.c:899 inside PointLineDist2D (pinned), and lbl_80345D50 is read throughout LineLineDist (pinned, two rules). config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json lists three pins for this unit across those two functions. Editing either body to spell the literal aborts the build - measured, not theorised: the D50-only conversion died with `ValueError: LineLineDist: input hash 313f3882... != expected 49596e08...`. So the flip needs those pins RETIRED FIRST, which re-exposes the allocator walls they cover. Note also that btricol's .sdata2 is ALREADY byte-identical to the target (0x30, all six entries), so unlike auxanim these two ghosts are pure duplicate spellings of pool entries MWCC already emits as @46/@48 - there is no data gain available, only the link-blocker removal. GENERAL LESSON, and the reason this class keeps surviving sweeps: see claim.law.own-pool-ghost-extern-flatters-fndiff-reloc-rows.20260831.v1 - the ghost makes the score look BETTER, so any score-gated cleanup pass rejects the correct fix. SHELF LIFE: this result is true as of 2026-08-31 at commit efa6d56df. Any future 'zero ghosts' claim must carry its measurement date and the object mtimes it was computed from; the screen costs ~30 seconds over 257 objects and should simply be re-run rather than cited.
